standard_prerequisites.name: Conditions, stabilisation of a stem and strong cone avoidance
standard_prerequisites.statement: The section works with conditions, each a triple of a colouring constrained by a computable bounding function, a finite stem and an infinite reservoir computing a fixed set D; a reservoir stabilises a stem when for each tuple of the stem and each length below the bounding function at the least element of the tuple the image of the reservoir on that length lands in a fixed finite set of short tuples of the stem; and the section proves separately a strong cone-avoidance statement for the finite-dimensional free-set principle, for colourings whose colours are finite sets rather than natural numbers, with the Catalan number as the bound on the number of colours. The author's own definitions and that proposition are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is the step that turns a condition into one whose reservoir stabilises the stem without leaving the cone of D, and it is invoked by every later step of the diagonalisation.

core_obligations: Derive a finite family of colourings of the reservoir indexed by the nonempty short tuples of the stem and by the lengths below the bounding function: each such colouring sends a finite subset of the reservoir to the intersection of the image of the set appended to the tuple with the stem, so its colours are the short tuples of the stem rather than natural numbers (source line 1149, first sentence).

Apply the strong cone-avoidance proposition for that finite-dimensional free-set principle with the colour set bounded by the Catalan number, finitely many times at once, to obtain one infinite subset of the reservoir that avoids the cone of the fixed set D and whose derived colourings all have strictly fewer than the Catalan number many values on sets of the relevant length (source line 1149, second sentence).

Read off stabilisation: collect for each index the union of the values of the derived colouring over all subsets of the chosen reservoir of the relevant length, check that this union is a finite set of short tuples of the stem whose size is at most the product of the bounding function at the least element of the tuple with the Catalan number, and conclude that the reservoir stabilises the stem by definition, while keeping the cone-avoidance property (source line 1149, third sentence).

proof_roadmap.step: Derive the colourings into short tuples of the stem, indexed by the tuples of the stem and the admissible lengths.
Iterate strong cone avoidance finitely many times for all derived colourings at once, keeping the cone of D avoided.
Collect the finite unions, bound their sizes and conclude stabilisation by definition.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2412.11598v3 的 Lemma lem:fs-stabilizing（源 1144-1147 行，证明 1148-1150 行）：对任意有限串 σ 与满足 max σ < min X、D ⩽̸_T X 的无穷集 X，存在无穷 Y ⊆ X 使 Y 稳定 σ（定义见 1138-1142 行）且 D ⩽̸_T Y。关键操作不是例行核验：证明要为每个非空 t ⊆ σ 与每个 n ≤ h(min t)−|t| 造出取值于 [σ]^{≤b_f(min t)}（**有限串集合**而非自然数）的导出着色 g_{t,n}(u)=f(t·u)∩σ（1149 行），再对**有限多**个着色一次性迭代强锥回避（且颜色数用 Catalan 数 C_n 界住），最后把每个 g_{t,n} 在 [Y]^n 上的像取并得到有限集 I_{t,n} 并核对 |I_{t,n}| ≤ b_f(min t)×C_n，从而按定义得到稳定化。难点在于颜色不再是自然数、必须把「像集大小被 C_n 界住」这一步接进强锥回避，同时保持 D 的锥被避开；原文位置在证明的 1149 行（该证明整段一段写就），引文 Cholak–Patey 与桩 6.8 各一处。

editorial_notes: The counted unit is the article's own Lemma lem:fs-stabilizing at source lines 1144-1147 together with its proof at source lines 1148-1150, a straight adjacent pairing in the pinned file. The pinned file is a concatenation of the authors' main and macro files; it is the article's fixed version arXiv:2412.11598v3 under CC BY 4.0.

This source ships no separate preamble file, so the retained preamble is sliced mechanically from the pinned file by the lane and is shared, byte for byte, with the other cards of this source; it carries the authors' full macro block so that no macro of a retained span is left undefined.

Three context spans make the section's standing material available: the convention at line 1119 that fixes the bounded-constrained colouring and its bounding function, the reminder at line 1135 that the symbol used in the statement and in the proof denotes the n-th Catalan number, and the author's definition at lines 1138-1142 of what it means for a set to stabilise a finite stem. All three are context, not counted units, and none of them overlaps the counted interval.

The retained proof quotes one proposition of the same article, the strong cone-avoidance statement whose own environment at line 1083 carries no proof; it is declared as a non-load-bearing navigation pointer with the article's own section-wise number 6.8, which the lane counted over the numbered environments of section 6.

The retained proof also cites the article on thin sets for reversely well-founded partial orders at source line 1149, where it invokes strong cone avoidance of the finite-dimensional free-set principle. That entry is supplied as a task-directory fragment holding it exactly as a bibtex run on the host had formatted it out of the article's own bibliography, since the bibtex backend cannot be used in this harness; the bibliography backend is therefore none.

The statement and proof of this lemma are written as a single paragraph by the author; nothing inside them is omitted and no part of the argument points at an unreproduced statement other than the two items above.
